adjacent_skills.you_have: Autonomous systems / CV robotics (turret, Jetson perception)

strengths: COFFIN capstone (Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm) is a genuine multi-component system-integration project — perception (TensorRT/YOLO), real-time control (servo IK on Arduino), sensor fusion (dual ToF), and a systemd-deployed service with static networking — directly maps to 'System Integration' and 'On-Robot Validation'

Robustness & reliability engineering has concrete backing: COFFIN's '11 integration failures resolved, 100% pick reliability' bullet and Robocon's fail-safe state machine / PWM-saturation debugging are exactly the kind of edge-case hardening the JD's 'Robustness & Reliability Engineering' bullet describes

Debugging & root cause analysis across software/sensors/timing/hardware is well backed — Robocon's interrupt-driven quadrature decoding and COFFIN's stale-frame/servo-brown-out fixes show cross-layer debugging, not just app-level

Strong C++/Python dual proficiency with real embedded C++ (Arduino IK, STM32 bare-metal) and Python (Flask-SocketIO, PyQt GUIs), matching the JD's 'read, debug, write production-level C++ alongside Python tooling' ask
real_gaps: No localization, state estimation, or SLAM anywhere in the profile — a named 'Robotics Software Fundamentals' bullet with zero backing
No outdoor or unstructured-environment deployment — every project is indoor/lab/bench/competition or pure simulation (CARLA); the JD's entire framing is outdoor industrial robots
No teleoperation experience — COFFIN's voice-command interface is an operator interface but not remote teleoperation of a mobile platform
No CI/CD, Docker, or Kubernetes anywhere in the profile — 'Tooling & Infrastructure' responsibility and two bonus quals are fully unbacked
No observability/diagnostics tooling (Foxglove, Grafana) — bonus qual with zero evidence
0 years full-time professional experience against the JD's 2+ year ask, though 7 internships partially offset this
overstated_by_keywords: 'Autonomous Vehicles' counted Adjacent, but the only evidence (CARLA) is simulation-only — no physical AV/drone/field hardware
'Controls' counted Have via PWM/servo closed-loop feedback — real, but RC/servo-level control, not a robot motion-planning/controls stack in the production-software sense the JD implies
understated_by_keywords: COFFIN's systemd deployment (auto-restart, non-root isolation, env-based config, static IP networking) is genuine production-deployment discipline the keyword pass under-weighted — it just doesn't use the literal words 'Docker' or 'CI/CD'

Robocon's real-time closed-loop heading correction and fail-safe halt-on-disconnect state machine is stronger 'field-like reliability under competition pressure' evidence than the keyword score credited
screening_gaps: No outdoor/unstructured-environment field deployment anywhere in the profile — RoboForce's entire product thesis is outdoor industrial robots, and every project here is indoor/lab/competition/simulation
Zero backing for localization or state estimation, a named robotics-fundamentals requirement
No CI/CD, Docker, or Kubernetes experience — the 'Tooling & Infrastructure' responsibility has no supporting evidence
llm_analysis.reasoning: The debugging, robustness, and hands-on hardware-integration depth (COFFIN, Robocon, Object Tracking Turret) genuinely map to half of the JD's core responsibilities, and the C++/Python/embedded/perception combination is real, not surface. But the profile has zero outdoor-deployment evidence against a company built entirely around outdoor field robots, no localization/state-estimation work, and no CI/CD or release-infrastructure experience — three gaps concrete enough that a recruiter reading closely would flag them, even though the underlying robotics fundamentals are solid enough to make this worth applying to as a stretch role.
